content.text:
I submitted **index 6 (In 0.79 / Sb 0.21)** as the best composition. It had the highest measured EQE, 0.079%. All 3 merit measurements are used; I used 3 of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Composition (In / Sb) | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.87 / 0.13 | 0.031 |
| **6** | **0.79 / 0.21** | **0.079** |
| 19 | 0.36 / 0.64 | 0.061 |

- **How I picked the samples:** the phase database lists three known In–Sb oxides: In11Sb3O24 near index 6, InSbO4 near index 15, and In3Sb5O12 near index 19. I measured index 6 and index 19 first. For the last measurement I took the Gaussian-process model's suggestion, index 0 at the In-rich end. It came out lowest, so the best result is at intermediate In content rather than at the In-rich edge.
- **Phase identification is uncertain:** the XRD patterns don't match any known phase well. Index 6 is closest to In11Sb3O24 and InSbO4, but the similarity is only about 0.35. Index 19 matches nothing above 0.21. So I can't say which crystal structure is behind the best result.
- **Coverage is thin:** with three measurements across 28 compositions, the peak could lie elsewhere. The largest untested gap is between index 6 and index 19, which includes the InSbO4 composition. The score counts only measured compositions, so index 6 is the result that stands.
